text:
Alex Carter: Quick thought — we should change default saved-query scope to be route-local first, but show an explicit team/org toggle in the saved dialog. Users keep asking why a saved view disappears when switching routes.
Maria Chen: +1. Route-local makes sense for most quick saves. But we need to make telemetry & quota implications visible up-front.
Jordan Patel: For the API, I propose adding a scope enum: `route | team | org` and a `telemetry_hint` field so the console can suggest sampling (low/medium/high). This avoids shipping a bunch of hidden telemetry spikes.
Samir Rao: API sketch looks fine. Example payload:
```
POST /v1/saved_queries
{
  "name": "Errory requests - 95th latency",
  "scope": "route",
  "route_id": "route_abc123",
  "model_id": "redwood/v1-16k",
  "query": "status:500 | p95(latency)",
  "telemetry_hint": "medium",
  "pinned": false
}
```
Lena Ortiz: UX: when scope!=route show a subtle badge in the list and a confirmation: "This saved view applies to X routes — affects telemetry & quota". Also show cost estimate per day/week if telemetry_hint is medium/high.
Alex Carter: Agree. Also add a little help tooltip: "Team-scoped views aggregate across routes and increase sampling/compute — consider route scope for targeted debugging."
Maria Chen: On rollout: do a canary where team/org-scoped saves are disabled for trial orgs, and we collect delta in telemetry (query counts, token-cost estimate). We'll gate full rollout on <10% cost delta and no perf regressions.
Jordan Patel: For quotas: saved queries with org scope should create a synthetic "saved_query-aggregate" telemetry bucket we can map to quota meters. That way billing/quotas and alerting can be clear.
Samir Rao: Implementation note — runtime routing needs to support pinned saved-queries that pre-warm prefix caches and batching rules. We'll need a lightweight precompile step when a team-scope saved query is created. Can we async that?
Maria Chen: Yes, async precompile + a status flag in the saved query object (precompiled:true/false) and a small background job that has backoff. Console should show spinner until ready.
Lena Ortiz: For the console list, let's add two new filter chips: Scope and Telemetry Hint. People can filter to only route-scoped saved queries. Keeps the list tidy.
Alex Carter: One more product constraint: retained saved queries should not change route-level defaults silently. If a team-scope query is later edited to route-scope, the console prompt must ask whether to replace route-local or create a new copy.
Jordan Patel: Devex ask: make the saved-queries API idempotent via client-supplied client_token. Also return a small diff when switching scopes so UI can present the change.
Samir Rao: I'll wire backend endpoints and background job. Plan: feature branch with basic API + precompile worker. Deploy to staging, then canary to 5 orgs.
deploy-bot: alex-carter triggered deploy of saved-query-api fea/sg-precompile to staging — build 2026.03.20-rc1 — succeeded.
Maria Chen: I'll draft console mockups: saved dialog with scope selector, telemetry hint dropdown, cost preview, and an inline explanation. Will post before EOD.
Lena Ortiz: UX checklist: badge for non-route scope, filter chips, cost preview, spinner for precompile, confirm-on-scope-change.
Alex Carter: OK good plan. Owners: Samir backend, Maria + Lena console, Jordan API contract, Alex product. Follow-up sync Friday 10am to review staging telemetry.
Jordan Patel: Also, let's add a lightweight telemetry metric `saved_query.created.{scope}` and `saved_query.used.{scope}` with sampling so we can monitor adoption without overloading metrics.
Maria Chen: makes sense — set sampling to 1% for org scope initially.
Samir Rao: Noted. I'll add to the job.
Alex Carter: Thanks all — I'll create the RFC doc and link it in #product after the mockups.
